newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 19.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
* Oracle Corp plans to acquire Navio Communications Inc, a unit of Netscape Communications Corp.
* ITT Corp is expected to announce plans to sell five of its Sheraton hotels to FelCor Suite Hotels Inc for $200 million in cash.
* The Clinton administration is expected to announce new rules designed to cut down on drug trafficking between Latin America and the U.S.
* McDonald's Corp plans to make sweeping changes to its top U.S. management structure in an effort to improve profits and increase market share.
* The Class of 1997 is finding a kinder, gentler job market in contrast to the grim outlook their parents faced as they graduated from college.
* Informix Corp has seen its stock drop as its financial condition has eroded and takeover bids have failed to materialize.
* The spate of consolidations that have taken place in the radio industry and the elimination of a tax credit have led to fewer stations being owned by minorities.
* Companies are hiring private detectives to protect their interests on the Internet.
* It's getting more complicated to tap into a site on the Internet. But the helps is there on, where else? The World Wide Web.
* Several advertising companies, including CKS Group Inc, have been looking to expand through acquisitions.
* Publishers of religious books are finding that novels that combine spiritual uplift with entertainment are also page-turners, as much as Bibles and devotional books.
* New York State is seeking to lure businesses to its borders by offering pollution credits to companies.
* Microsoft Corp, which has dominated the personal computer market, is now setting its sights on large-scale computer chores, such as payrolls and manufacturing.
* Stories about tackling Mount Everest have turned into an entertainment boon from books to movies.
* Newspapers, facing declining readerships, are changing their formats to try to connect with readers and reverse the trend.
